summary: ICIS (Oct 2): PP yarn/inj flat at low end, -USD 30 at high end to 1,270-1,300 CFR; BOPP -10 to 1,300-1,330
Domestic plants aligned: north NSRP 114G / BSR T3034 VND 39,500-40,000/kg incl VAT (flat)
Sellers lift Chinese/Korean homo & Sabic copo +VND 500-700/kg as volumes thin; buyers wait for post-Oct 7 China
paras: According to ICIS assessments released on last week's final trading day, October 2, the general PP yarn/injection price level in Vietnam last week held flat at the low end but fell USD 30/tonne at the high end, ranging USD 1,270-1,300/tonne/CFR; BOPP film prices fell USD 10/tonne from a week earlier, to USD 1,300-1,330/tonne/CFR.

Trading activity in Southeast Asia remained limited amid volatile crude oil prices and the risk of renewed tension escalation in the Middle East. Spot supply in the region remained limited and priced above normal.

Buyers expect this scarcity may ease in October. One reason is that some Chinese suppliers may look to export as their inventories build up in October — largely because buyers in that country have finished restocking ahead of the extended National Day holiday. Moreover, some previously contracted cargoes are expected to arrive in October after delays.

For the Vietnamese market, import offers early this week were quiet because Chinese suppliers are on holiday, while offers from some other producers such as Sabic and IRPC are too high. One source said IRPC (Thailand) offers PP yarn/injection at USD 1,540/tonne/CFR and PP Film 1126NK at USD 1,630/tonne/CFR…, with only customers needing the exact specified grades inquiring.

In domestic trading, a survey today found most sellers holding PP prices flat from late last week. In the north, offer levels for domestically sourced PP yarn such as NSRP's 114G and BSR's T3034 commonly ranged VND 39,500-40,000/kg including VAT. In the south, BSR's PP yarn T3034 and Hyosung Vina's PP yarn F501 commonly settled at VND 39,500/kg including VAT… Offer prices for PP from domestic plants are thus fairly aligned.

Imported PP homopolymer of Chinese and Korean origin was commonly in the VND 38,500-40,000/kg including VAT range depending on grade and distributor. Notably, last week some northern sellers offered Sabic PP copolymer 36MK10, 37MK10 and 310MK10 at only VND 38,000-38,500/kg including VAT, and South Korea's SK PP homopolymer at only VND 37,500/kg including VAT and SK PP random at VND 38,500/kg including VAT… but today they raised each grade by about VND 500-700/kg, as remaining volumes have fallen considerably.
At the higher end, a southern distributor offered Thailand's IRPC PP 1102K at VND 44,000/kg including VAT and IRPC PP Film 1126NK at up to VND 45,500/kg including VAT…

“Trading sentiment in the resin market this week is generally quite subdued and cautious; both sellers and buyers are waiting for adjustments from the Chinese market after the holiday ends on October 7 to gauge the October trend more clearly,” a source said.

summary: ICIS (Oct 2): LLDPE 1,250-1,320 CFR (+20 low/-10 high); HDPE Film 1,270-1,340 (+30/+15); LDPE Film flat 1,490-1,600
Spot LLDPE Film held flat — Mid-East VND 42-43k, US-origin ~41-41.5k; LDPE eased to 45,000-45,500/kg
Tasnee offered LDPE Film 1,550-1,565 CFR; Basell LDPE settled 1,540-1,580 CIF; Lotte HDPE 1,340, Sinopec HDPE yarn 1,300
paras: According to ICIS assessments released on last week's final trading day, October 2, the general LDPE Film price level in Vietnam last week held flat from the week before at USD 1,490-1,600/tonne/CFR; LLDPE rose USD 20/tonne at the low end but fell USD 10/tonne at the high end, ranging USD 1,250-1,320/tonne/CFR; HDPE Film rose USD 30/tonne at the low end and USD 15/tonne at the high end, to USD 1,270-1,340/tonne/CFR; while HDPE injection and blow both held flat, at USD 1,170-1,200 and USD 1,200-1,230/tonne/CFR respectively.

Across the wider region, negotiation activity in China was subdued last week as the National Day holiday began midweek (October 1). Lower-priced US cargoes are expected to arrive in port in October, so the current scarcity of spot supply may gradually ease. The market expects demand to keep softening after the holiday, but with no early sign of an end to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, the trend remains hard to predict.

In Southeast Asia, import market price levels moved in mixed directions, with some ranges narrowing amid prolonged uncertainty over cargoes from the Middle East, while crude oil and feedstock prices kept fluctuating without a clear trend. China's spot and futures markets being closed for most of the week also left Southeast Asian market participants somewhat disoriented, limiting trading volumes even though some key suppliers had announced monthly offers early in the week. Some suppliers in Southeast Asia also lowered their offers as buyer sentiment showed signs of stalling.

Today, October 5, on the first trading day of the new week, trading was not yet truly lively, as suppliers were cautious about price adjustments with China on holiday and the Middle East tensions developing in a complex manner.

A survey found Middle Eastern-origin PE such as Sabic and Qamar (Saudi Arabia) still scarce for prompt delivery; PE cargoes from China originally expected for September delivery were mostly still delayed; while US-origin PE import cargoes are expected to arrive from this week.

In domestic trading, spot LLDPE Film offers mostly held flat late last week due to limited volumes; Middle Eastern-origin LLDPE Film was commonly in the VND 42,000-43,000/kg including VAT range, while US-origin LLDPE Film was also offered at a high level of around VND 41,000-41,500/kg including VAT.

Even so, LDPE Film transaction prices eased slightly. Last week, many sellers raised offers for LDPE Film of Sabic, Tasnee, Lotte Titan, PTT… origin to VND 46,000-48,000/kg including VAT; however, according to a northern source today, transaction prices were commonly in the VND 45,000-45,500/kg including VAT range…

For HDPE, offers for Chinese-origin HDPE Film have come down to VND 39,000/kg including VAT, but offers for Middle Eastern-origin HDPE Film held at a high VND 41,000-43,000/kg including VAT; offers for HDPE yarn/blow grades were also commonly in this range…

On imports, late last week the distributor of Saudi Arabia's Tasnee offered Tasnee LDPE Film grades 1925AS/4025AS to Vietnam at USD 1,550/tonne/CFR and LDPE Film 0725N at USD 1,565/tonne/CFR, for a total offered LDPE volume of more than 1,000 tonnes. The distributor also offered HDPE injection IM2050 to Vietnam at USD 1,300/tonne/CFR and HDPE 100 black at USD 1,325/tonne/CFR…, with HDPE volumes offered smaller than LDPE. Cargoes are for November 2026 delivery.

Basell's distributor announced settled prices for LDPE Film to Vietnamese buyers of USD 1,580/tonne/CIF for orders under 100 tonnes, USD 1,560/tonne/CIF for orders of 50-100 tonnes, and USD 1,540/tonne/CIF for orders above 100 tonnes.
Meanwhile, South Korea's Lotte settled HDPE Film/yarn with Vietnamese buyers late last week at USD 1,340/tonne/CIF, and China's Sinopec settled HDPE yarn at USD 1,300/tonne/CIF…

summary: AGC (ASC/AVT Oct cargoes) at USD 825-830 CIF, -25-30 vs two weeks ago; trading still thin
Shintech (US) lifted SE950/SE1000 bid to 790-800 CIF (+~20) on Oct-Nov plant maintenance plans
Sept PVC imports >81,000 t at ~USD 740 avg; cheap US SE950/SE1000 (620-650) keep arriving, capping Oct upside
paras: ThitruongHatnhua.com (Oct 5) — Imported PVC prices into Vietnam are mixed: US-origin offers were adjusted up while other Asian supply stays under pressure from weak buying demand.

AGC Group's distributor settled October 2026 PVC cargoes from Ashahimas Indonesia (ASC) and Vinythai Thailand (AVT) at USD 825-830/tonne CIF for Vietnamese buyers, down USD 25-30/tonne from offers two weeks earlier. Actual trading volume remained thin, suggesting buyers are not yet restocking aggressively despite the lower adjustment.

Conversely, Shintech (US) raised its bid for PVC SE950/SE1000 delivered to Vietnam to USD 790-800/tonne CIF, up about USD 20/tonne from early last month. Cargoes are expected to arrive in January 2027. The higher level is supported by Shintech's plan to idle some PVC plants for maintenance in October-November 2026, raising supply concerns ahead.

Domestically, Shintech (US) PVC SE950 rose VND 300/kg to VND 24,500-25,000/kg at buyers' warehouses in Hanoi, up 1.23% from the prior week-end (Oct 2). All other PVC grades in the price table held steady.

On supply, Vietnam imported more than 81,000 tonnes of PVC in September at an average import price of about USD 740/tonne. Notably, a significant volume of US-origin PVC SE950/SE1000 contracted earlier at around USD 620-650/tonne continues to arrive in October.

This low-priced inflow may add competitive pressure to the domestic market while end-demand has yet to truly improve. Hence, even though some US PVC offers are rising on supply factors, the domestic PVC price level in October is still unlikely to climb sharply.
